properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 2:07AM MST until November 4 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, major flooding is occurring along the lower
Animas River. Water levels are approaching those experienced during
the great flood of October 1911.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 AM MST Tuesday the stage was 13.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 AM MST Tuesday was 13.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is near crest and is expected to fall below
flood stage around midnight and continue falling.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon MST.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 3 at 2:05AM MST until November 3 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Havasu Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 900 AM MST Tuesday.

* At 205 AM MST, a river gauge on Cataract Creek reported a rapid
rise of 5.38 feet as a result of heavy rain far upstream. A flood
wave is traveling through Cataract/Havasu Creek. Estimated time for
impacts to begin at Supai is between 9 AM to noon MST, though this
may change. Stay tuned to future updates for refinements on this
estimate.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Havasu Creek basin.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Havasu Creek basin.

* For Cataract Creek at Cataract Creek Below Heather Wash:
At 1:30am the stage was 4.46 feet.
Flood Stage is 7.5 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: 450 cfs flow. May cause minor flooding downstream in
Supai campground 4 to 7 hours later.
At 10.0 feet: 1520 cfs flow. May cause moderate flooding downstream
in Suapi village 4 to 7 hours later.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Supai, Havasupai Reservation, Little Navajo Falls, Mooney Falls and
Beaver Falls.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Very Last Chance Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Heather Wash, Sinyella Canyon, Little Coyote Canyon, Pasture Wash,
Havasu Creek, Black Tank Wash, Colorado River and Coconino Wash.
properties.instruction:
Campers and hikers should hustle to higher ground immediately! Stay
away from creeks and washes!

Foot bridges will be washed out in Supai Campground. Some campsites
will be flooded. Campers may be stranded in portions of the
campground.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 2 at 8:49PM PST until November 3 at 9:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

Mancos River near Mancos affecting Montezuma County.

.Moderate flooding will continue along the Mancos River as excess
runoff moves downstream.

For the Mancos River...including Mancos...Moderate flooding is
occurring.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring with a stage of 8.1 feet near
Mancos. The river is forecast to drop into the minor flood stage by
midnight and below bankfull by Tuesday evening.

* WHERE...Mancos River near Mancos and downstream.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, residential flooding in Mancos is likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM MST Monday the stage was 8.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:00 PM MST Monday was 8.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 4.4 feet late Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Heed any evacuation orders from local authorities.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday evening at 1015 PM MST.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 5:39PM MST until November 4 at 5:49PM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

San Juan River At Shiprock affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant impacts are likely in the Shiprock area and
along the San Juan River from Shiprock to the Four Corners.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 PM MST Monday the stage was 18.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:00 PM MST Monday was 18.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.3 feet
late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage early Wednesday
morning.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be alert to the forecast and obey all evacuation orders from local
authorities.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 600 AM MST.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 4:44PM MST until November 3 at 10:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Woodruff to Leupp...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 436 PM MST, water levels have begin to fall near Woodruff and
Holbrook, but both remain above flood stage. Water levels at
Winslow remain above major flood stage, and are expected to rise
through the overnight as elevated flow moves downstream. Flooding
will continue to remain a threat downstream of Winslow in the
Birdsprings area as well. Flooding is already ongoing.
- For the Little Colorado River near Woodruff:
At 4:30pm MST the stage was 21.71 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: Water levels have crested and are expected to fall
through this evening.
Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Bankfull. Portions of residential yards flooded.
- For the Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 20.27 feet is expected at 5:00pm MST Monday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.
At 25.0 feet: Levee overtopped. Major flooding.
- For the Little Colorado River at Joseph City:
At 4:30pm MST the stage was 6.73 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 8.09 feet is expected this evening.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.
At 9.0 feet: Flood stage. Minor overflow on right (north) bank,
with no threat to any buildings, mainly rural countryside.
- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 4:00pm MST the stage was 25.25 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 39.94 feet is expected at 4:00am MST
Tuesday.
Impacts:
At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank
to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure.
At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of
Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Woodruff, Bushman Acres, Homolovi
Ruins State Park, Rosedale Heights, and Clearview Heights.


- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

* WHERE...La Plata River below Redmesa.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...The La Plata River is impacting the bridge over Pinon
Hills near Farmington and homes are being inundated along the
river.

- At 3:30 PM MST Monday the stage was 9.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM MST Monday was 10.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain in flood stage through
late tonight.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood

properties.headline: Gale Warning issued November 1 at 3:33PM AKST until November 3 at 5:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Offshore waters forecast for the Gulf of Alaska West of 144W

Wind forecasts reflect the predominant speed and direction
expected. Sea forecasts represent an average of the highest
one-third of the combined wind wave and swell height.

.TONIGHT...S wind up to 10 kt. Seas 7 ft. Rain showers. Isolated
thunderstorms.
.MON...S wind up to 15 kt increasing to 10 to 25 kt in the
afternoon. Seas 5 to 8 ft.
.MON NIGHT...SE wind 25 to 40 kt. Seas 6 to 11 ft building to 9 to
17 ft after midnight. Rain.
.TUE...SE wind 30 to 45 kt. Seas 13 to 20 ft.
.TUE NIGHT...S wind 15 to 30 kt. Seas 13 to 20 ft.
.WED...SE wind 15 to 25 kt. Seas 11 to 14 ft.
.THU THROUGH FRI...SE wind 20 to 35 kt. Seas 13 to 21 ft.
